resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]Logical Operators [/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

Logical operators [b]&&[/b] and [b]||[/b] are used to form a compound Boolean expression that tests multiple conditions. A third logical operator is [b]![/b] used to reverse the state of a Boolean expression.

[h2]The && Operator [/h2]
The logical AND operator [b]&&[/b] returns a true result only when both expressions are true.
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="c" codeId="1645"]if (n > 0 [b]&&[/b] n <= 100)
  printf("Range (1 - 100).\n"); [/code]
The statement above joins just two expressions, but logical operators can be used to join multiple expressions.
A compound Boolean expression is evaluated from [b]left to right[/b]. Evaluation stops when no further test is needed for determining the result, so be sure to consider the arrangement of operands when one result affects the outcome of a later result.
[note]Run the code and see how it works![/note]

resolved.title: 逻辑或 || 运算符
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]The || Operator[/h1][/s0l0!-header] 

The logical OR operator [b]||[/b] returns a true result when any one expression or both expressions are true. 
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="c" codeId="1646"]if (n == 'x' || n == 'X')
  printf("Roman numeral value 10.\n"); [/code]
Any number of expressions can be joined by && and ||. 
[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="c" codeId="1647"]if (n == 999 || (n > 0 && n <= 100))
  printf("Input valid.\n"); [/code]
[note]Parentheses are used for clarity even though && has higher precedence than || and will be evaluated first.[/note]

resolved.title: 非运算符 ！
resolved.description:
[s0l0!-header][h1]The ! Operator[/h1][/s0l0!-header]

The logical NOT operator [b]![/b] returns the reverse of its value. 
NOT true returns false, and NOT false returns true.

[s0l0!-header][b]For example:[/b][/s0l0!-header] [code format="c" codeId="1648"]if ([b]![/b](n == 'x' || n == 'X'))
  printf("Roman numeral is not 10.\n"); [/code]
[note]In C, any non-zero value is considered [b]true [/b]and a 0 is [b]false[/b]. The logical NOT operator therefore, converts a true value to 0 and a false value to 1.[/note]
